channel.title: cs.CL updates on arXiv.org
channel.description: cs.CL updates on the arXiv.org e-print archive.

item.title: Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00001v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural networks store many concepts in superposition, which makes single neurons hard to read. We train sparse autoencoders on residual stream activations and find that the learned dictionary features are far more interpretable than neurons, as judged by automatic and human evaluation. We also show that the features can be used to localize and edit the behavior of a circuit responsible for indirect object identification.
item.dc:creator: Hoagy Cunningham, Aidan Ewart, Logan Riggs, Robert Huben, Lee Sharkey

item.title: Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders
item.description: arXiv:2609.00002v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how sparse autoencoder quality scales with dictionary size and training compute. A k-sparse activation removes the need for an L1 penalty and gives a clean tradeoff between reconstruction and sparsity. We propose several metrics for feature quality and release a 16 million latent autoencoder trained on GPT-4 activations.
item.dc:creator: Leo Gao, Tom Dupre la Tour, Henk Tillman, Gabriel Goh, Rajan Troll, Alec Radford, Ilya Sutskever, Jan Leike, Jeffrey Wu

item.title: Interpretability in the Wild: a Circuit for Indirect Object Identification in GPT-2 small
item.description: arXiv:2609.00003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We reverse engineer the mechanism GPT-2 small uses to complete sentences such as 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to'. The circuit involves 26 attention heads grouped into seven classes, discovered with causal interventions such as path patching. We propose faithfulness, completeness and minimality as criteria for evaluating a mechanistic explanation.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Wang, Alexandre Variengien, Arthur Conmy, Buck Shlegeris, Jacob Steinhardt

item.title: Steering Llama 2 via Contrastive Activation Addition
item.description: arXiv:2609.00004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce contrastive activation addition, a method for steering language models by adding a vector to the residual stream at inference time. Steering vectors are computed from the difference in activations between positive and negative examples of a behavior. The approach modulates sycophancy, hallucination and refusal in Llama 2 with little loss of capability.
item.dc:creator: Nina Rimsky, Nick Gabrieli, Julia Schulz, Meg Tong, Evan Hubinger, Alexander Matt Turner

item.title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
item.description: arXiv:2609.00005v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe representation engineering, which places population-level representations rather than neurons or circuits at the center of analysis. Reading and controlling these representations gives traction on honesty, harmlessness and power seeking, and provides a complement to bottom-up mechanistic interpretability.
item.dc:creator: Andy Zou, Long Phan, Sarah Chen, James Campbell, Phillip Guo, Richard Ren, Alexander Pan, Xuwang Yin, Mantas Mazeika, Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski

item.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2609.00006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A task vector is the difference between the weights of a fine-tuned model and its pre-trained base. We show that task vectors can be negated to forget a behavior, added to merge abilities from several fine-tuned models, and combined by analogy. Task arithmetic is a cheap and effective way to edit models without further training.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Ilharco, Marco Tulio Ribeiro, Mitchell Wortsman, Suchin Gururangan, Ludwig Schmidt, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Ali Farhadi

item.title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00007v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model merging combines several task-specific fine-tuned models into one multitask model without retraining. We identify two sources of interference, redundant parameter values and sign disagreement, and propose TIES-Merging, which trims parameters, elects a sign and merges only agreeing values. The method outperforms prior merging methods across modalities and model sizes.
item.dc:creator: Prateek Yadav, Derek Tam, Leshem Choshen, Colin Raffel, Mohit Bansal

item.title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
item.description: arXiv:2609.00008v1 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that most delta parameters of a fine-tuned language model can be dropped without hurting performance. Drop And REscale (DARE) randomly sets delta parameters to zero and rescales the rest, which makes it possible to merge several fine-tuned models into one model that absorbs their abilities.
item.dc:creator: Le Yu, Bowen Yu, Haiyang Yu, Fei Huang, Yongbin Li

item.title: Who's Harry Potter? Approximate Unlearning in LLMs
item.description: arXiv:2609.00009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a technique for unlearning a subset of the training data from a large language model without retraining from scratch. Fine-tuning Llama2-7b for about one GPU hour removes its ability to generate or recall Harry Potter related content while keeping performance on common benchmarks. We discuss the difficulty of evaluating machine unlearning.
item.dc:creator: Ronen Eldan, Mark Russinovich

item.title: TOFU: A Task of Fictitious Unlearning for LLMs
item.description: arXiv:2609.00010v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose TOFU, a benchmark for machine unlearning built from fictitious author profiles that no model has seen during pretraining. The benchmark measures forget quality and model utility after unlearning. Existing unlearning methods fail to match a model retrained without the forget set.
item.dc:creator: Pratyush Maini, Zhili Feng, Avi Schwarzschild, Zachary C. Lipton, J. Zico Kolter

item.title: The WMDP Benchmark: Measuring and Reducing Malicious Use With Unlearning
item.description: arXiv:2609.00011v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We release the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy benchmark, a set of multiple-choice questions that serve as a proxy for hazardous knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity and chemistry. We also introduce RMU, an unlearning method based on steering model representations, which reduces hazardous knowledge while preserving general capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Nathaniel Li, Alexander Pan, Anjali Gopal, Summer Yue, Daniel Berrios, Alice Gatti, Justin D. Li, Ann-Kathrin Dombrowski, Shashwat Goel, Long Phan

item.title: A Watermark for Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a watermarking framework for proprietary language models that embeds an invisible signal in generated text. The watermark selects a randomized set of green tokens before each word is sampled and softly promotes them. Detection needs no access to the model and works from a short span of tokens, with a statistical test and interpretable p-values.
item.dc:creator: John Kirchenbauer, Jonas Geiping, Yuxin Wen, Jonathan Katz, Ian Miers, Tom Goldstein

item.title: Can Watermarks Survive Translation? On the Cross-lingual Consistency of Text Watermark for Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Text watermarks for large language models are usually evaluated in one language. We introduce cross-lingual consistency, the ability of a watermark to remain detectable after the text is translated into another language, and find that current watermarking methods lose almost all of their strength under translation. We propose a cross-lingual watermark removal attack and a defense that shares watermark keys across semantically equivalent tokens in multiple languages.
item.dc:creator: Zhiwei He, Binglin Zhou, Hongkun Hao, Aiwei Liu, Xing Wang, Zhaopeng Tu, Zhuosheng Zhang, Rui Wang

item.title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction
item.description: arXiv:2609.00014v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Across 13 open chat models we find that refusal is mediated by a single one-dimensional subspace of the residual stream. Ablating this direction removes refusal, and adding it induces refusal on harmless requests. We use the finding for a white-box jailbreak that edits weights and discuss implications for the robustness of safety fine-tuning.
item.dc:creator: Andy Arditi, Oscar Obeso, Aaquib Syed, Daniel Paleka, Nina Panickssery, Wes Gurnee, Neel Nanda

item.title: Gemma Scope: Open Sparse Autoencoders Everywhere All At Once on Gemma 2
item.description: arXiv:2609.00015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sparse autoencoders are an unsupervised method for learning a sparse decomposition of the latent representations of a neural network. Training a comprehensive suite of them is expensive, so we release Gemma Scope, JumpReLU sparse autoencoders trained on every layer and sublayer of the Gemma 2 2B and 9B models, to accelerate interpretability research.
item.dc:creator: Tom Lieberum, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Arthur Conmy, Lewis Smith, Nicolas Sonnerat, Vikrant Varma, Janos Kramar, Anca Dragan, Rohin Shah, Neel Nanda

item.title: Attribution Patching Outperforms Automated Circuit Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2609.00016v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated circuit discovery methods such as ACDC are slow because they require a forward pass per edge. We show that a linear approximation, attribution patching, estimates edge importance with a single backward pass and recovers circuits at least as faithful as those from ACDC on standard tasks at a fraction of the cost.
item.dc:creator: Aaquib Syed, Can Rager, Arthur Conmy

item.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
item.description: arXiv:2609.00017v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mechanistic interpretability work follows a workflow of choosing a task, a metric and a granularity, then pruning the model to find the subgraph that implements the behavior. We automate the pruning step with ACDC, an algorithm that recovers previously published circuits in GPT-2 small, including the indirect object identification circuit.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Conmy, Augustine N. Mavor-Parker, Aengus Lynch, Stefan Heimersheim, Adria Garriga-Alonso

item.title: Do Llamas Work in English? On the Latent Language of Multilingual Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2609.00018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We ask whether multilingual language models use English as an internal pivot language. Applying the logit lens to Llama 2 on translation and cloze prompts in several languages, we find that intermediate layers assign high probability to the English version of the next token before the final layers commit to the target language. We discuss what this means for cross-lingual bias.
item.dc:creator: Chris Wendler, Veniamin Veselovsky, Giovanni Monea, Robert West

item.title: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
item.description: arXiv:2609.00019v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce inference-time intervention, which shifts activations along truth-related directions in a small number of attention heads during decoding. The method raises the truthfulness of Llama on TruthfulQA from 32.5 to 65.1 percent with only a few hundred labeled examples, and is a form of activation steering that is cheap to apply.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Li, Oam Patel, Fernanda Viegas, Hanspeter Pfister, Martin Wattenberg

item.title: Model Stock: All we need is just a few fine-tuned models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00020v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We observe that fine-tuned weights from different random seeds lie close to a thin shell around a center, and that performance improves as weights approach that center. Model Stock estimates the center from only two fine-tuned models and the pretrained model, which gives a merging method with negligible cost.
item.dc:creator: Dong-Hwan Jang, Sangdoo Yun, Dongyoon Han

item.title: Large Language Models for Code: Security Hardening and Adversarial Testing
item.description: arXiv:2609.00021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Code language models often generate insecure code. We propose controlled code generation, in which a property prefix steers the model toward secure or, for adversarial testing, vulnerable code, and implement it with a learned prefix that does not modify the model weights.
item.dc:creator: Jingxuan He, Martin Vechev

item.title: Locating and Editing Factual Associations in GPT
item.description: arXiv:2609.00022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze how factual associations are stored in GPT models using causal tracing, and find that mid-layer feed-forward modules at the subject token play a decisive role. Rank-One Model Editing (ROME) changes a single fact by modifying one such module, which we evaluate on a new counterfactual dataset.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Meng, David Bau, Alex Andonian, Yonatan Belinkov

item.title: Toy Models of Superposition
item.description: arXiv:2609.00023v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neural networks often represent more features than they have dimensions by storing them in superposition. We study small toy models where this is fully understood, show that superposition depends on feature sparsity and importance, and connect the geometry of the learned representations to the difficulty of mechanistic interpretability.
item.dc:creator: Nelson Elhage, Tristan Hume, Catherine Olsson, Nicholas Schiefer, Tom Henighan, Shauna Kravec, Zac Hatfield-Dodds, Robert Lasenby, Dawn Drain, Carol Chen

item.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
item.description: arXiv:2609.00024v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Induction heads are attention heads that implement a copy-and-complete pattern. We present evidence that the formation of induction heads during training accounts for most in-context learning in small transformers, and give weaker circumstantial evidence for the same claim in large models.
item.dc:creator: Catherine Olsson, Nelson Elhage, Neel Nanda, Nicholas Joseph, Nova DasSarma, Tom Henighan, Ben Mann, Amanda Askell, Yuntao Bai, Anna Chen

item.title: Transcoders Find Interpretable LLM Feature Circuits
item.description: arXiv:2609.00025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Circuit analysis through MLP sublayers is hard because they are dense and nonlinear. Transcoders approximate an MLP with a wider, sparse layer whose features are interpretable, which lets us do weights-based circuit analysis and recover the greater-than circuit in GPT-2 small without input-dependent approximations.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Dunefsky, Philippe Chlenski, Neel Nanda

item.title: Function Vectors in Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00026v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We find that a small set of attention heads carries a compact representation of the task demonstrated in an in-context prompt. Averaging their outputs gives a function vector that triggers the task in a zero-shot setting, and function vectors can be added together to compose tasks.
item.dc:creator: Eric Todd, Millicent L. Li, Arnab Sen Sharma, Aaron Mueller, Byron C. Wallace, David Bau

item.title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning for Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00027v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We survey machine unlearning for large language models, where the goal is to remove the influence of unwanted data or capabilities while keeping everything else. We connect unlearning to model editing, influence functions and adversarial training, discuss evaluation, and list open problems such as the tension between forgetting and utility.
item.dc:creator: Sijia Liu, Yuanshun Yao, Jinghan Jia, Stephen Casper, Nathalie Baracaldo, Peter Hase, Yuguang Yao, Chris Yuhao Liu, Xiaojun Xu, Hang Li

item.title: Negative Preference Optimization: From Catastrophic Collapse to Effective Unlearning
item.description: arXiv:2609.00028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gradient ascent on the forget set collapses model utility. We propose negative preference optimization, a loss inspired by preference optimization that uses only negative examples, and show it unlearns TOFU authors far more effectively while preserving utility on the retain set.
item.dc:creator: Ruiqi Zhang, Licong Lin, Yu Bai, Song Mei

item.title: Three Bricks to Consolidate Watermarks for Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consolidate watermarking for language models with three contributions: statistical tests with guaranteed false positive rates, evaluation on natural language and code generation tasks, and a multi-bit variant that identifies the model or the user who produced the text.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Fernandez, Antoine Chaffin, Karim Tit, Vivien Chappelier, Teddy Furon

item.title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
item.description: arXiv:2609.00030v1 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chain-of-thought explanations can misrepresent the true reason for a prediction. We bias inputs, for example by always placing the correct answer as option A in few-shot demonstrations, and find that models rationalize the biased answer without mentioning the bias.
item.dc:creator: Miles Turpin, Julian Michael, Ethan Perez, Samuel R. Bowman

item.title: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present high quality image synthesis with diffusion probabilistic models, a class of latent variable models inspired by nonequilibrium thermodynamics. Training uses a weighted variational bound that connects diffusion models to denoising score matching and Langevin dynamics, and yields strong results on CIFAR10 and LSUN.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Ho, Ajay Jain, Pieter Abbeel

item.title: High-Resolution Image Synthesis with Latent Diffusion Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: By running diffusion in the latent space of a pretrained autoencoder we reach a near-optimal point between complexity reduction and detail preservation, which lowers the compute needed for training and sampling. Cross-attention layers turn the model into a flexible conditional generator for text-to-image and inpainting.
item.dc:creator: Robin Rombach, Andreas Blattmann, Dominik Lorenz, Patrick Esser, Bjorn Ommer

item.title: Segment Anything
item.description: arXiv:2609.00033v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a promptable image segmentation model, a dataset of more than one billion masks on 11 million images, and a data engine that produced it. The model transfers zero-shot to new image distributions and tasks.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Kirillov, Eric Mintun, Nikhila Ravi, Hanzi Mao, Chloe Rolland, Laura Gustafson, Tete Xiao, Spencer Whitehead, Alexander C. Berg, Wan-Yen Lo

item.title: CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages
item.description: arXiv:2609.00034v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: CodeBERT is a bimodal pre-trained model for programming language and natural language, trained with masked language modeling and replaced token detection on NL-PL pairs. It reaches strong results on natural language code search and code documentation generation and is a useful base for program comprehension research.
item.dc:creator: Zhangyin Feng, Daya Guo, Duyu Tang, Nan Duan, Xiaocheng Feng, Ming Gong, Linjun Shou, Bing Qin, Ting Liu, Daxin Jiang

item.title: Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code
item.description: arXiv:2609.00035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Codex, a GPT model fine-tuned on public code, and HumanEval, a set of hand-written programming problems that measure functional correctness. We discuss limitations such as difficulty with long chains of operations, and the safety and economic implications of code generation.
item.dc:creator: Mark Chen, Jerry Tworek, Heewoo Jun, Qiming Yuan, Henrique Ponde de Oliveira Pinto, Jared Kaplan, Harri Edwards, Yuri Burda, Nicholas Joseph, Greg Brockman

item.title: Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00036v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We find an adversarial suffix that, appended to a range of queries, makes aligned language models produce objectionable content. The suffix is found by greedy and gradient-based search and transfers from open models to black-box commercial chat models.
item.dc:creator: Andy Zou, Zifan Wang, Nicholas Carlini, Milad Nasr, J. Zico Kolter, Matt Fredrikson

item.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00037v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We demonstrate a training data extraction attack that recovers verbatim sequences from the training set of GPT-2, including personal information, by querying the model. Larger models are more vulnerable, and we discuss possible mitigations.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Carlini, Florian Tramer, Eric Wallace, Matthew Jagielski, Ariel Herbert-Voss, Katherine Lee, Adam Roberts, Tom Brown, Dawn Song, Ulfar Erlingsson

item.title: Are Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models a Mirage?
item.description: arXiv:2609.00038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Claimed emergent abilities may be artifacts of nonlinear or discontinuous metrics rather than fundamental changes in model behavior. We show that with linear or continuous metrics the same models display smooth, predictable improvements with scale.
item.dc:creator: Rylan Schaeffer, Brando Miranda, Sanmi Koyejo

item.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
item.description: arXiv:2609.00039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We analyze performance on multi-document question answering and key-value retrieval as the position of relevant information varies. Performance is highest when relevant information is at the beginning or end of the context and drops significantly in the middle, even for models designed for long contexts.
item.dc:creator: Nelson F. Liu, Kevin Lin, John Hewitt, Ashwin Paranjape, Michele Bevilacqua, Fabio Petroni, Percy Liang

item.title: Direct Preference Optimization: Your Language Model is Secretly a Reward Model
item.description: arXiv:2609.00040v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We derive a closed form for the optimal policy under the RLHF objective, which turns preference learning into a simple classification loss on the language model itself. DPO is stable, lightweight and matches or exceeds PPO-based RLHF on sentiment control, summarization and dialogue.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Rafailov, Archit Sharma, Eric Mitchell, Stefano Ermon, Christopher D. Manning, Chelsea Finn

item.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00041v1 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We freeze pretrained weights and inject trainable rank decomposition matrices into each layer of the transformer. LoRA reduces trainable parameters by 10,000 times and GPU memory by three times compared to full fine-tuning while matching quality on GPT-3.
item.dc:creator: Edward J. Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang, Weizhu Chen

item.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Providing a few chain of thought demonstrations as exemplars in prompting improves the ability of large language models to perform arithmetic, commonsense and symbolic reasoning. Gains are largest for the largest models and appear to be an emergent property of scale.
item.dc:creator: Jason Wei, Xuezhi Wang, Dale Schuurmans, Maarten Bosma, Brian Ichter, Fei Xia, Ed Chi, Quoc Le, Denny Zhou

item.title: The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget
item.description: arXiv:2609.00043v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that training on model-generated data causes irreversible defects in the resulting models, which we call model collapse. The tails of the original content distribution disappear, and we show the effect in language models, variational autoencoders and Gaussian mixture models.
item.dc:creator: Ilia Shumailov, Zakhar Shumaylov, Yiren Zhao, Yarin Gal, Nicolas Papernot, Ross Anderson

item.title: Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning at Scale
item.description: arXiv:2609.00044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We train a transformer-based masked language model on one hundred languages using more than two terabytes of filtered CommonCrawl data. XLM-R improves over multilingual BERT on cross-lingual classification, sequence labeling and question answering, and we analyze the curse of multilinguality.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Conneau, Kartikay Khandelwal, Naman Goyal, Vishrav Chaudhary, Guillaume Wenzek, Francisco Guzman, Edouard Grave, Myle Ott, Luke Zettlemoyer, Veselin Stoyanov

item.title: No Language Left Behind: Scaling Human-Centered Machine Translation
item.description: arXiv:2609.00045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We build a conditional compute model based on a sparsely gated mixture of experts, trained on data obtained with novel mining techniques for low-resource languages, and evaluate translation across 40,000 directions with a human-translated benchmark, FLORES-200.
item.dc:creator: NLLB Team, Marta R. Costa-jussa, James Cross, Onur Celebi, Maha Elbayad, Kenneth Heafield, Kevin Heffernan, Elahe Kalbassi, Janice Lam, Daniel Licht

item.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
item.description: arXiv:2609.00046v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SWE-bench contains 2,294 software engineering problems drawn from real GitHub issues and pull requests across twelve Python repositories. Given a codebase and an issue description, a model must produce a patch that passes the tests. The best models resolve only a small fraction of the tasks.
item.dc:creator: Carlos E. Jimenez, John Yang, Alexander Wettig, Shunyu Yao, Kexin Pei, Ofir Press, Karthik Narasimhan

item.title: Model Editing Can Hurt General Abilities of Large Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00047v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We evaluate models after factual editing on reasoning, question answering, code generation and other general tasks, and find that many editing methods degrade these abilities, especially as the number of sequential edits grows.
item.dc:creator: Jia-Chen Gu, Hao-Xiang Xu, Jun-Yu Ma, Pan Lu, Zhen-Hua Ling, Kai-Wei Chang, Nanyun Peng

item.title: Mechanistic Interpretability for AI Safety: A Review
item.description: arXiv:2609.00048v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We review mechanistic interpretability, the project of reverse engineering the computational mechanisms of neural networks into human-understandable algorithms. We cover features, circuits, superposition, probing, sparse autoencoders and causal methods, and discuss how the field relates to AI safety.
item.dc:creator: Leonard Bereska, Efstratios Gavves

item.title: Not All Language Model Features Are Linear
item.description: arXiv:2609.00049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The linear representation hypothesis proposes that features are one-dimensional directions. We use sparse autoencoders to find multi-dimensional features in GPT-2 and Mistral 7B, including circular representations of days of the week and months of the year, and show with intervention experiments that the model uses them for modular arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Engels, Eric J. Michaud, Isaac Liao, Wes Gurnee, Max Tegmark

item.title: The Geometry of Truth: Emergent Linear Structure in Large Language Model Representations of True/False Datasets
item.description: arXiv:2609.00050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We curate datasets of simple true and false statements and show that language model representations of them have linear structure. Probes trained on one dataset generalize to others, and the truth direction can be used to causally steer the model toward treating false statements as true.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Marks, Max Tegmark

item.title: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition
item.description: arXiv:2609.00051v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present a residual learning framework that eases the training of networks that are much deeper than before. Layers learn residual functions with reference to the layer inputs, and on ImageNet we evaluate residual nets with a depth of up to 152 layers.
item.dc:creator: Kaiming He, Xiangyu Zhang, Shaoqing Ren, Jian Sun

item.title: Textbooks Are All You Need
item.description: arXiv:2609.00052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce phi-1, a 1.3 billion parameter code language model trained on textbook quality data from the web and synthetically generated textbooks and exercises. Despite its small size it reaches strong pass@1 accuracy on HumanEval and MBPP.
item.dc:creator: Suriya Gunasekar, Yi Zhang, Jyoti Aneja, Caio Cesar Teodoro Mendes, Allie Del Giorno, Sivakanth Gopi, Mojan Javaheripi, Piero Kauffmann, Gustavo de Rosa, Olli Saarikivi

item.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2609.00053v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study empirical scaling laws for language model performance on the cross-entropy loss. Loss scales as a power law with model size, dataset size and compute, with trends spanning more than seven orders of magnitude, and larger models are significantly more sample efficient.
item.dc:creator: Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Tom Henighan, Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Chess, Rewon Child, Scott Gray, Alec Radford, Jeffrey Wu, Dario Amodei

item.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners
item.description: arXiv:2609.00054v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, and test its performance in the few-shot setting. GPT-3 achieves strong performance on many NLP datasets, including translation, question answering and cloze tasks, without gradient updates or fine-tuning.
item.dc:creator: Tom B. Brown, Benjamin Mann, Nick Ryder, Melanie Subbiah, Jared Kaplan, Prafulla Dhariwal, Arvind Neelakantan, Pranav Shyam, Girish Sastry, Amanda Askell

item.title: Poisoning Web-Scale Training Datasets is Practical
item.description: arXiv:2609.00055v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce two attacks that guarantee malicious examples land in web-scale datasets: split-view poisoning, which exploits the mutable content behind published URLs, and frontrunning poisoning, which targets datasets that snapshot crowd-sourced content such as Wikipedia.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Carlini, Matthew Jagielski, Christopher A. Choquette-Choo, Daniel Paleka, Will Pearce, Hyrum Anderson, Andreas Terzis, Kurt Thomas, Florian Tramer
